sentences.text: 1 Heard on IA No..8729/2022, an application for condonation of delay of 46 days in filing the appeal.
After due consideration, the same is allowed and delay in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.
IA is disposed off accordingly.
With the consent of both the parties, the matter is heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 11.03.2022 passed by 3rd Additional MACT, District Bhopal in MACC No.1466 of 2016 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that nature of injuries sustained by the appellant has been diagnosed as simple but life threatening.
Appellant remained admitted for seventeen days and he was admitted twice.

Tribunal has awarded only Rs.43,700/- for loss of income during treatment,
pain and suffering, attendant charges, conveyance charges etc.
Tribunal has not awarded any amount for future treatment.
Hence, compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company has submitted that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
Hence, appeal filed by appellant be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.
6. Perusal of impugned award reveals that no permanent disability certificate has been filed on behalf of the appellant and there are no medical documents requiring future medical treatment.

Hence, no amount can be awarded for under above heads.
7.
It is correct that appellant has remained admitted for 17 days in the Hospital and has been admitted twice in the Hospital.
It is also correct that appellant has suffered serious injuries in intestine.
8.In view of above, compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads ie. Rs.43,700/- is enhanced to Rs.55,000/-.
9. Enhanced amount of (Rs.55,000/- - Rs.43,700/-) = Rs.11,300/- shall carry interest at the rate awarded by the Tribunal.
Other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
10. Appeal partly allowed to the extent as indicated above.
(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE vai Hukum Singh Bhopa @ Karan vs Prakhar Dubey
